title: mcp 0.4.0
text: Multiple regression: mcp now supports several continuous predictors, categorical predictors, interactions, etc. terms RHS. E.g., ~ 1 + x + x:state + sigma(1 + state) + ar(2, 0 + z). Basically, now aims “feels” like lm() glm() distributional parameter segment. Explore ex = mcp_example("multiple") see action read Understanding mcp formulas. Default priors follow rstanarm brms possible. possibility parameters also comes convenient () share coefficients across segments - including categorical predictors group-level effects (read ). Group-level effects RHS: Predictor formulas now support group-level effects (random effects) using familiar lme4 brms syntax. (1 | group) specifies group-level intercept, (1 + x || group) (factor || group) support independent coefficients, including slopes factors. also works inside distributional formulas sigma(1 + (factor || id)). See mcp_example("group_mu") article group-level effects worked examples. Correlated multi-coefficient terms yet supported. Native feel: mcpfits now work natively R generics, posterior tidybayes posterior draw prediction API. Changes include: summary(fit) now reports rank-normalized split-rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail posterior central quantile intervals instead HDIs. Adding as_draws(fit), as_draws_df(fit), tidy_draws(fit), ndraws(fit), variables(fit), posterior_epred(fit), posterior_predict(fit), posterior_linpred(fit), loo_compare(), etc. full S3 generic registration posterior, rstantools, tidybayes (spread_draws(), gather_draws()). bayesplot::mcmc_trace(fit) etc. work now. Per-draw methods (summary = FALSE fitted(), predict(), residuals(), log_lik()) now return dot-prefixed columns (.epred, .prediction, .residual, .loglik) tidybayes / ggdist compatibility. fitted() returns .linpred scale = "linear" [.dpar] dpars (e.g., .sigma, .ar1, mu). See Fits predictions. nsamples soft-deprecated favor ndraws; which_y deprecated favor dpar. Added R generics mcpfits: formula(fit), family(fit), model.frame(fit), nobs(fit), vcov(fit), confint(fit), coef(fit). lme4 brms, coef() returns absolute group-specific coefficients change points, ranef() returns relative deviations. Fits now also store proper matched $call. Printed summaries now report posterior sd new layout. Dirichlet now default prior change points: one-change-point models, prior identical v0.3.4. default change point prior now mathematically beautiful principled Dirichlet prior, previously supported secondary option. uniform order statistics, .e., uniform priors change points, restricted observed data range, cp_i = "dunif(min(x), max(x))", ordered: cp_1 < cp_2 < .... ordering, results scaled beta prior change point. See formal description . dunif()-specification new default, old cp_i = "dirichlet(alpha)" syntax remains supported (see breaking changes ). New: set minimum segment length, e.g., cp_2 = "dunif(cp_1 + 20, max(x))". models 2+ change points, previous sequentially truncated t-distributions centered min(x) removed. Truncated-t served purpose higher ESS/s expense mathematically unprincipled. new implementation JAGS makes fast. Although mathematical change, parameter posteriors remain essentially identical previous fits mcp_example(). hypothesis(fit, "cp_1 = 20") (Savage-Dickey Bayes Factor) default priors likely differ, BF ill advised default priors anyway - hypothesis() now throws warning attempted. Negative binomial offset(): can now mcp(..., family = negbinomial()). NB (Poisson) can now model rates exposure offset() now supported formulas - also families. one segment includes offset(), segments must include one. See Poisson negative-binomial article applied example. Missing response imputation: Missing responses now retained posterior JAGS imputations used complete response histories AR/MA models. Predictions generate fresh replicated outcomes every row; predict(fit) |> filter(.na(y)) can used see predictive intervals draws missing points, similarly fitted() expected responses. Missing AR/MA histories remain unsupported log_lik(), loo(), waic(). See article missing data. Improved speed robustness: ESS/s improved 10-fold convergence likely. due reparameterizations keep intercepts slopes relatively independent earlier segments sampling due (selectively) using JAGS glm module. reparameterizations change model priors.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: mcp v0.4 major breaking change aim remaining relatively stable going forward towards version 1.0. Although lot updated, parameter estimates v0.4.0 remain practically identical previous public release (v0.3.4). Deprecation detections added reach 1.0. Renamed parameters column names align brms: int_i –> Intercept_i; x_1_E2 –> xE2_1; x_1_sin –> sinx_1, cp_1_sd –> cp_1_id_sd ((1 | id)), etc. Interactions join parts dot, e.g., x:stateB –> x.stateB_1. Renamed return column names align posterior others: summary(), fixef(), ranef() now name parameter identifier column parameter instead name, matching prior_summary() mcp_pars(). fitted(), predict(), residuals(), log_lik() summary = TRUE now take width = 0.95 instead probs (deprecated warning) return columns .mean, .sd, .lower, .upper instead fitted/predict/residuals/loglik, error, Q2.5, Q97.5. matches summary() (width, mean, sd, lower, upper), dot prefix prevents collisions data columns, broom::augment(). Consequently, data columns named sd, fitted, predict, etc. longer rejected. quantiles, summarise draws summary = FALSE. evaluation-row key data_row now .row, matching tidybayes. plot(fit, q_fit, q_predict) deprecated favor plot(fit, interval = c("fitted", "predict"), width = 0.95). matches new width summary(), fitted(), predict(). Add quantiles ggplot2 layer fitted(..., summary = FALSE) instead. Rhat renamed rhat summary(), fixef(), ranef(), match posterior standard. hypothesis() returns column prob instead p posterior (prior) probability directional hypotheses, preventing confusion frequentist p-values. also returns posterior sd hypothesis, like summary(). Change points modeled using cp(): Segments 2+ now one-sided formulas, change points modeled using cp(), e.g., list(y ~ 1, ~ cp((1 | id)) + 0 + x) instead list(y ~ 1, 1 + (1 | id) ~ 0 + x). avoids confusing left-hand side response variable. old syntax deprecated works warning shows new formula. formula(fit) summary(fit) show new syntax. Parameters outputs: fit$pars fit$mcmc_loglik removed now raises helpful errors. fit$pars now replaced mcp_pars(fit) mcp_columns(fit). fit$mcmc_loglik longer stored - generate using log_lik(fit). mcp:::tidy_samples() removed. Use as_draws_df(fit) tidybayes::spread_draws(). fixef() now reports population-level effects mu (primary response parameter), excluding change points, distributional parameters, AR/MA parameters, group-effect SDs. Use summary(fit) get parameters. general, renamed "varying" "group", e.g., now plot_pars(fit, pars = "group") fitted(fit, group_effects = "x_2_id"). varying deprecated alias warning. summary(), fixef(), ranef(), prior_summary(), as_draws(), fit$prior, fit$simulate(), everything else now order parameters canonically mcp_pars() instead previous incidental (near-alphabetical) order; group levels follow grouping factor’s levels fitting data. Draws fitted(), predict(), etc. summary = FALSE ordered data row, draw, tidybayes. Use verbose = TRUE summary(), fixef(), ranef() include segment dpar columns. Tibbles generally returned instead data.frame() readability. Tibbles data frames, x[, "col"] now returns one-column tibble instead vector. Use x$col x[["col"]] get vector. change involves summary(), fixef(), ranef(), fitted(), predict(), residuals(), hypothesis(), interpolate_newdata(). mcp longer exports phi, logit, ilogit, probit. Functions, plotting, workflow: plot() now split plot() plotting full fits plot_dpar() plots one distributional parameter (mu, sigma, shape, ar1, etc.). argument order changed . new coloring function (plot(fit, color_by = "column")) particularly useful models include categorical predictors rhs group-level effects. default color_by = "auto" colors sole categorical predictor. See mcp_example("group_mu") plotting article worked examples. Parallel sampling now controlled exclusively active future plan. cores argument mcp() deprecated ignored, remains available backwards compatibility. Use future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 3) calling mcp() sample chains parallel, future::plan(future::sequential) shut workers. Without parallel future plan, chains sampled sequentially. Chain-specific initial values (inits = list(list(...), list(...))) now supported parallel execution supplying explicit seed. Binomial predictions now default counts: fitted() returns expected successes predict() returns predicted successes (rate = FALSE), matching posterior_epred(), posterior_predict(), brms. v0.3.4 methods defaulted proportions. Update old scripts explicit rate = TRUE retain proportions, rate = FALSE select counts. omitted rate warns per session per function requested counts differ proportions. ar(p) longer continues later segments: terms included segment get coefficients . important new multiple-regression functionality, backward incompatibility model like model = list(y ~ 1 + ar(1), ~ 0), AR continue segment 2. equivalent model v0.4+ ~ 0 + ar(1, 0) segment 2. Explicit prior draw selection: Methods requiring draws now require posterior draws default error unavailable. Use prior = TRUE select prior draws; prior-fits longer trigger automatic fallback. also applies draw-count methods, print(fit) shows model unless prior = TRUE. arguments fit$simulate() changed accommodate multiple (categorical) predictors. fit$simulate(fit, newdata, ..., .type = "predict") new argument structure. Note (1) now requires fit first argument, (2) requires data.frame tibble second argument instead just vector par_x, (3) arguments prefixed “.” avoid name conflicts internally mcp. ... model parameters usual. fit$simulate() now also preserve shared group effects specified priors (e.g., prior = list(Intercept_2_id = "Intercept_1_id")). hypothesis() takes fit first argument x (fit), matching brms::hypothesis(). now restricts equality tests simple parameter contrasts gives clearer guidance Savage-Dickey Bayes factors. Non-linear transformations hypotheses like x_1 / x_2 = 1 previously run, even though Savage-Dickey support . Equality tests now return prob = NA Bayes factor model comparison, posterior parameter probability. Density estimates robust, warn evaluating Savage-Dickey Bayes factors default priors, warn sparse tails. See Savage-Dickey Bayes factors. mcp(..., adapt = 1000) soft-deprecated favor mcp(..., warmup = 1000) compatibility additional future samplers. Formula modeling semantics: Dropped support rel() formulas. ambiguous interaction terms made code hard maintain. Compute relative changes posterior draws shown Relative changes segments. Dropped support mcp(..., data = NULL). now must provide mock-data inform mcp types levels predictor columns. See, e.g., mcp_example("intercepts")$example_code simple example mcp_example("multiple")$example_code involved example. docs updated appropriately. Gaussian models explicit sigma() formula now model residual standard deviation log link, brms. make scale visible, intercepts named sigma_Intercept_i (previously sigma_i), matching Intercept_i, slopes keep names (e.g., sigma_x_2) now log scale. Models without explicit sigma() unchanged: sigma_1 remains residual SD response-scale half-Student-t prior. See distributional parameters. y | weights(w) now specifies observation log-likelihood weights rather Gaussian-precision weights (previously scaled residual SD sigma / sqrt(w)). Unlike brms, weights must strictly positive due JAGS requirements (zero). Predictive draws expectations now use distribution parameters directly log_lik() multiplies observation log-densities w. Formula transformations now use original predictor values, lm(), glm(), brms. Previously, transformations change-point predictor sin(x) exp(x) restarted change point. Bare par_x polynomial bases (par_x^2) still measured change point support joined segments. Fitting priors: prior user-specified priors 2+ change points differ mcp v0.3.4, though informative data, posteriors highly similar. User-specified priors change points now used unchanged, though restricted ordered change points. v0.3.4 imposed ordering truncating priors using T() previous change point, e.g., dnorm(40, 10) T(cp_1, max(x)), pushed wide priors towards max(x). dunif() priors priors T() used unchanged, allowed label switching. Fixed change points, e.g., cp_2 = 80, now ordered relative change points . Priors without dunif() T() truncated observed range x. See priors change points. lower upper bounds change point priors, .e., arguments dunif() T(), can longer refer change points, except set minimum segment length, e.g., cp_2 = "dunif(cp_1 + 20, max(x))". Change points distribution’s parameters remain allowed, e.g., cp_3 = "dnorm(cp_2 + 30, 10)". dirichlet(alpha) now takes one shared alpha >= 1 (non-integer allowed) change points applies segments, including last. v0.3.4 allowed non-identical integer alpha per change point silently used alpha = 1 last segment, dirichlet(2) now gives different prior. Non-identical alphas now error. Group-level change points (1|id) now use standard hierarchical normal model sampled efficiently absolute locations. makes cp_i_sd SD normal distribution truncation rather realized sample SD. default prior group-level change-point SDs (cp_i_id_sd) now dnorm(0, (max(x) - min(x)) / (2 * (n_cp() + 1))) T(0, ), .e., quarter expected interval group’s change point can vary. old prior, group-level change points barely pooled, cp_i cp_i_id_sd weakly identified. new prior approximately uniform realized SD group-level change points, differs cp_i_id_sd, SD truncation. See default priors justification. AR MA intercepts now zero-centered, regularizing dnorm(0, 0.5) T(-1, 1) priors, replacing independent uniform priors. categorical contrasts numeric slopes now use modest normal priors instead heavy-tailed Student-t priors. Coefficients remain direct jointly constrained stationary invertible regions (read ). Corrected JAGS translation prior scales. ddexp() dlogis() now convert conventional scale inverse scale rather inverse variance; exported sd_to_prec() helper soft-deprecated prior translation now internal, sampler-specific step.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: Generalized AR/MA: Autoregression (ar()) generalized link-scale observation-driven GARMA residuals Gaussian, binomial, Bernoulli, Poisson, negative-binomial models default links, using ar(..., threshold = 0.1) default keep observations finite link scale. Added moving-average terms ma(q), can used alone combined ar(p) segment. Independent time series can separated using ar(..., series = <column>). Set series threshold ar() ma() term; apply segments. See article time series. GARMA observation thresholds now validated support response: strictly 0.5 family = bernoulli(), strictly half smallest trial count family = binomial(), preventing thresholds erasing binary response history. Explicit AR/MA prediction history control: predict() new posterior_predict() support arma = "replicate" generate fresh response series recursively, addition arma = TRUE (default) condition observed response histories arma = FALSE omit AR/MA effects. applies prior posterior prediction. Previously, AR history handling depended whether response values supplied. Added AR/MA warnings: (1) AR/MA models loo(), predict(), etc. serial dependence currently ignored. Proper handling requires leave-future-blocked cross-validation, currently implemented mcp. (2) posterior violation probabilities exceed configurable ar ma diagnostic thresholds (10% default). New features mcp(): Added warnings various thresholds exceeded. mcp(..., diagnostics = list(rhat = 1.01, ess_bulk = 400, ess_tail = 400, ar = 0.10, ma = 0.10)) controls fit diagnostics configurable thresholds. Partial lists override defaults, individual diagnostics can disabled NULL, diagnostics = FALSE disables diagnostic warnings. summary(fit) inherits settings accepts override diagnostic footer. Use mcp(..., seed = 42) set.seed(42) mcp() reproducible JAGS sampling, whether chains run sequentially parallel. See mcp_example("demo")$example_code ensure reproducibility across simulation, fit, plotting. mcp(..., quiet = TRUE) suppresses routine JAGS output mcp sampling-status messages preserving warnings errors. Use options(mcp_quiet = TRUE) make default session. JAGS model-compilation text longer printed default. fit$version records versions mcp, R, rjags, JAGS used make fit, e.g., fit$version$mcp >= "0.4.0". Memory improvement: mcpfit now < 10% size log-likelihood stored. Use log_lik(fit) compute , call loo(fit) waic(fit) directly. Model evaluation prediction: Added log_lik(fit) returns draws--observation matrix default. usual brms return shape accepted directly loo. log_lik() supports arguments e.g. fitted(). Methods like fitted() predict() now select group-level effects using group_effects (previously varying). group_effects = FALSE NA gives population-level predictions, "cp" "predictor" select group-level effects formula part, parameter names accept * wildcards, e.g., fitted(fit, group_effects = c("cp_*", "state*_1_id")). ranef() continues return group-level effects. Fits made custom jags_code now warn calling R-side simulation, prediction, model-evaluation methods, methods continue evaluate supplied formulas rather custom JAGS code. jags_code planned deprecation future release brings custom families tooling run jags_code directly JAGS. need , please open issue describing use case. fitted(), predict(), residuals(), log_lik(), loo(), etc. now memory efficient (e.g., ~2.5 GB instead ~12 GB 2000 observations). Use loo(fit, ndraws = 1000) compute LOO subset draws. Priors hypotheses: Added prior_summary(fit). compact output shows parameter’s resolved prior lower upper bounds, marking change points ordered; prior_summary(fit, verbose = TRUE) also shows data-dependent rule, plain-language description, source, kind (distribution, alias, expression, constant). See Working priors. introduction multiple regression including categorical predictors (including distributional parameters) come default priors. Coefficients autoscaled rstanarm, .e., divided SD model-matrix column (see “Priors distributions” ). See prior_summary(fit, verbose = TRUE) details. Added option test hypotheses prior using hypothesis(fit, prior = TRUE). y | weights(w_col) now supported families (gaussian(), binomial(), bernoulli(), poisson(), negbinomial()). Applies log-likelihood weights brms. Plotting examples: Default plot(fit) style updated many ways accommodate multiple regression group-effects. Predictive intervals (plot(fit, q_predict = TRUE) predict(fit, summary = TRUE)) now precise faster. used estimated posterior parameter draws, MC error. Added interpolate_newdata(fit, = NULL) generates data.frame combinations categorical predictors along interpolated continuous predictors. Use include grouping factors. documentation shows can useful generating custom plots simple tweaking plot() enough. mcp_example(...) now shows illustrative plot fitted example default. Disable using plot = FALSE. New help topics ?mcp-formula (model formulas underlying model) ?mcp-priors (prior syntax), split ?mcp.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: Priors distributions: Default coefficient priors now follow autoscaled defaults rstanarm: normal(0, 2.5 * sd(y) / sd(x)) identity links normal(0, 2.5 / sd(x)) log links, sd(x) standard deviation predictor’s model-matrix column, including dummy variables factors. change-point variable, sd(x) taken data (slope priors depend number change points), powers (x^2) use sd((x - min(x))^2), interactions x:z use sd(x) * sd(z) (just sd(x) 0/1 dummies x:state). Version 0.3.4 used dt(0, sd(y) / (max(x) - min(x)), 3) Gaussian slopes, 9 times narrower evenly spread x noticeably shrank steep slopes short segments. Intercepts also follow rstanarm (normal(mean(y), 2.5 * sd(y)) Gaussian models), default prior segment-1 intercept applies level min(x), just rstanarm brms place intercept priors centered predictors. Intercept_1 still reported x = 0, lm(), fit$prior prior_summary() show prior given x-terms, e.g., dnorm(mean(y) - x_1 * min(x), 2.5 * sd(y)). greatly improves sampling x far zero, e.g., calendar years. Likewise factor levels contrasts x-terms, e.g., stateb_1 y ~ 1 + state * x. sigma group-level SDs follow brms. See priors using prior_summary(fit, verbose = TRUE) read default priors. implicit Gaussian sigma_1 prior now response-calibrated half-Student-t used brms, dt(0, max(2.5, round(mad(y), 1)), 3) T(0, ). Version 0.3.4 instead used response-SD-calibrated half-normal prior. weakly informative negligible impact fits. Uppercase data-dependent constants priors (MINX, MAXX, etc.) remain temporarily supported deprecation warning. now replaced readable expressions min(time), max(time) - min(time), mad(response), n_segments(), n_cp(). Priors can longer refer internal JAGS nodes cp_0 cp_K (e.g., cp_3 two change points). Use min(x) max(x) instead, also shown fit$prior. Binomial Bernoulli models logit probit links now use narrower, weakly regularizing scales rstanarm’s 2.5: normal(0, 1.5) (logit) normal(0, 1) (probit) intercepts, approximately exactly uniform probability scale, respectively. Coefficients categorical contrasts use normal(0, 1.5 / sd(x)) normal(0, 1 / sd(x)). See justification. Gaussian models log link (gaussian(link = "log")): Now aligned mcp’s general log-link model standards (dnorm rather Student-t reduce extreme multiplicative tails exponentiation). Population intercepts robustly calibrated empirical log-data (non-positive values replaced 0.1, brms zeros) shift offset(), coefficients categorical contrasts use rstanarm’s dnorm(0, 2.5 / sd(x)). Count model priors (poisson(), negbinomial()): v0.3.4, log-link Poisson models used uncalibrated, unscaled dnorm(0, 10) intercepts slopes. v0.4.0, population log-mean intercepts now robustly data-calibrated dnorm(median(log(y)), ...) (zeros replaced 0.1, brms) minimum scale 2.5, automatically shift observed log-rate (\log(y) - \text{offset}) offset() present (calibrating location scale directly rates, unlike brms, subtracts mean(offset) location computes scale log-counts). Coefficients categorical contrasts now use rstanarm’s dnorm(0, 2.5 / sd(x)). new RHS group-level features v0.4.0, group SDs default dnorm(0, 2.5) T(0, ) (scaled half-normals). Broad normal priors follow precedent rstanarm, substantially reducing extreme multiplicative effects explosive prior simulations compared Student-t priors exponentiation. Similarly, modeled log-shape negative-binomial (shape(...)) uses dnorm(0, 2.5) dnorm(0, 2.5 / sd(x)) rather Student-t priors (read ). Interface data structures: fit = mcp_example("name") now returns fit directly instead list $fit entry. now defaults sampling model (sample = "post") sample argument now directly passed mcp(..., sample = sample) sample = TRUE deprecated. term “ct” (“central tendency”) replaced dpar = "epred" (default), e.g., plot_dpar(fit, dpar = "epred") fitted(fit, dpar = "epred"). Deprecated which_y = "ct" translated dpar = "epred" warning. mcp(..., inits) can set parameters mcp_pars(fit) errors names. Parameters reparameterized faster sampling can longer initialized. Initial values change points must ordered (read ). fit$data now contains data columns used model. draws_format replaces samples_format fitted(), predict(), log_lik(). old argument remains available soft deprecation. residuals() now also takes draws_format, e.g., residuals(fit, summary = FALSE, draws_format = "matrix") draws--observation matrix like brms. Removed which_y argument predict(). rate = TRUE fitted(), predict(), plot() now errors families binomial Bernoulli. v0.3.4, silently ignored. rates per unit exposure models offset(log(exposure)), set exposure 1, e.g., fitted(fit, newdata = transform(df, exposure = 1)). loo() waic() always evaluate fitted model, including group-level effects AR/MA terms. Use log_lik(fit, group_effects = FALSE) log_lik(fit, arma = FALSE) conditional log-likelihoods. Additionally, loo(ndraws = ...) waic(ndraws = ...) now thin draws evenly across chains preserve MCMC chain identities order. New mcpfit objects longer include empty $loo $waic components. .mcpfit() deprecated favor is_mcpfit(), matching posterior’s is_draws(). Requirements removals: mcp now requires R >= 4.1.0, matching use native pipe (|>). Removed criterion() get_segment_table(). now throw error pointing replacements: loo(fit) waic(fit) instead criterion(fit), mcp_pars(fit) mcp_columns(fit) fit = mcp(..., sample = FALSE) instead get_segment_table(). Removed non-functional exponential() family. default priors fitted. Exponential survival models require dedicated support censoring survival likelihoods rather previous ordinary-response placeholder.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: Equality hypotheses now warn prior draws lie one side tested value: kernel smoothing can otherwise give misleading Bayes factors values outside prior bounds. Boundary tests receive warning; Bayes factor calculations unchanged. Named arguments prior distributions truncations (e.g. dnorm(sd = 1, mean = 10)) now rejected explicitly informative error rather silently re-interpreted positionally. hypothesis(..., prior = TRUE) now reports BF = NA rather comparing prior draws returning Bayes factor 1. Directional Bayes factors now divide posterior odds prior odds. Previously, reported posterior odds alone, Bayes factor prior probability hypothesis 0.5. residuals() now uses conventional observed - fitted sign. Previously, mcp residuals used fitted - observed. Poisson negative binomial predictions longer fail single draw implies count mean 2,146,275,819. common prior predictions default log-link priors. Fixed several posterior predictive check information-criterion bugs present v0.3.4. least serious: missing data: Missing responses scored WAIC/LOO JAGS-imputed values observed. Fix: missing responses remain latent JAGS excluded observed-data PPC, log-likelihood, WAIC, LOO calculations. models group-level change points, LOO checks facet_by != NULL pair group-specific predictions weights wrong observations. AR/MA models, pp_check() conditioned every prediction observed response history. now defaults arma = "replicate", generating posterior replication recursively fresh time series. Use arma = TRUE previous one-step-ahead check. LOO predictive checks keep arma = TRUE match one-step-ahead log-likelihood behind weights. LOO checks prior = TRUE incorrectly combined prior predictions posterior LOO weights. rare use case. pp_check(..., ndraws = NULL) errored. Fixed. text: Get fits predictions -sample --sample data. Read article functions. Use predict(fit) get predicted values quantiles. Use fitted(fit) get estimated values quantiles.
